This input is not a perfect square, so it has no exact integer root. What does the subject say to return then, and what does yours return instead: the root of a nearby square?
Can a number below zero ever be a perfect square? The subject returns a root "if it exists": does one exist here, and what does yours return?

Every answer here fits in an int, and so does nb. Does anything your code computes on the way to the answer grow past what its type holds on some platform? (What C promises about the width of each type: docs/testing.md, under ilp32.)
